questions.question: Which Mauryan Indian emperor is renowned for his edicts and pillars?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Ashoka**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Emperor Ashoka of the Mauryan Empire is renowned for his edicts and pillars:**
 
• Ashoka's edicts were inscriptions carved into stone pillars, boulders, and cave walls throughout India.
 
• These edicts provided insights into ancient India's history, culture, and governance.
 
• They included:
 
 
• Prohibition of animal sacrifice, especially during festive seasons
 
• Medical treatment of humans and animals
 
• Planting of fruits, medicinal herbs, and the digging of wells
 
 
 
• Ashoka's **edicts were made on the Pillars of Ashoka**.
 
• Ashoka ruled most of the Indian subcontinent from 268 BCE to 232 BCE.
 
• He was a highly influential promulgator of Indian Buddhism.
 
• His dhamma emphasized non-violence, mutual respect, and understanding between people of different sects and beliefs. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Harsha:
 
 
• Harsha, the ruler of the Vardhana dynasty (7th century CE), did issue coins, but they were primarily gold coins with his portrait, and he is famous for his patronage of Buddhism.
 
• His coins were more symbolic of his royal authority and religious support.
 
 
 
• Kanishka:
 
 
• Kanishka was a king of the Kushana dynasty (1st-2nd century CE), and he is one of the most prominent rulers known for issuing gold dinars.
 
• Kanishka’s gold coins were highly valued and important for the Kushana Empire's economy. T
 
• he coins featured various gods and symbols, and Kanishka was one of the key promoters of Buddhism.
 
 
 
• Samudragupta:
 
 
• Samudragupta, a ruler of the Gupta dynasty (4th-5th century CE), is famous for his gold coins.
 
• He is also known as a patron of the arts and for his military prowess.
 
• However, his coins were somewhat different in design, often depicting him as a warrior or seated in various poses of victory.

questions.question: Executive power of an Indian State is vested in ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The executive power of an Indian state is vested in the Governor:
 
• Governor
 
• The Governor is the head of the state and exercises executive power directly or through subordinate officers.
 
• The President of India appoints the Governor for a five-year term.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Council of Ministers
 
 
• The Council of Ministers is a body of advisors to the Governor, led by the Chief Minister.
 
• The Council of Ministers advises the Governor on governance matters and is responsible for administering the state.
 
 
 
• Chief Minister
 
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the elected government in a state and is responsible for administering the state.
 
 
 
• The Governor appoints the Chief Minister, who holds office at the Governor's pleasure.

questions.question: Addition to the stock of capital of a firm is known as __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Investment**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The addition to a firm's capital stock is known as an investment.
 
• Investment is the process of purchasing assets to generate income or appreciation in the future.
 
• It can also be referred to as capital formation. 
 
• Investment is a broader concept than capital formation, which is the accounting value of new non-financial assets added to the capital stock.
 
• Investment can include all types of capital assets, such as physical property or financial assets. 
 
• Investing is the act of allocating resources, usually capital, with the expectation of generating an income, profit, or gains. Investors typically consider that a greater period of time, like months or years, is needed to generate acceptable returns. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Accumulation
 
 
• Accumulation refers to the process of gathering or increasing resources, assets, or wealth over time. It can apply to financial savings, investments, or even physical goods.
 
• In Economics: It is often associated with the gradual build-up of capital or wealth through saving and reinvesting profits.
 
• Example: A person saving money in a bank account over several years is an example of wealth accumulation.
 
 
 
• Capital Loss
 
 
• A capital loss occurs when the value of an asset decreases, and it is sold for less than its original purchase price.
 
• In Economics/Finance: It is the opposite of a capital gain and often impacts a firm's or individual's financial health negatively.
 
• Example: Selling a property for ₹8 lakh when it was purchased for ₹10 lakh results in a ₹2 lakh capital loss.
 
 
 
• Capital Gain
 
 
• A capital gain occurs when an asset increases in value and is sold for more than its original purchase price.
 
• In Economics/Finance: Capital gains are often taxable and are a common source of income for investors.
 
• Example: Selling stocks for ₹5 lakh that were purchased for ₹3 lakh results in a ₹2 lakh capital gain.

questions.question: Which government of India program provides 100 days of wage employment to households in rural areas to ensure livelihood security?

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee scheme

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee (MGNREGA) scheme is a government of India program that provides a minimum of 100 days of wage employment to rural households in a financial year.
 
• The scheme was launched in 2006 to improve the livelihood security of rural households. 
 
• To be eligible for the MGNREGA scheme, an applicant must: Be an Indian citizen, Be at least 18 years old, Live in a rural area, and Be willing to do unskilled manual work. 
 
• Applicants can apply for a job card at their local Gram Panchayat.
 
• Once an application is submitted, the applicant should receive a job offer within 15 days.
 
• The applicant's wages are deposited directly into their bank account or post office account. 
 
• The central government pays for 100% of the unskilled labour costs and 75% of the material costs. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)
 
 
• A scheme by the Ministry of Rural Development to help poor families in rural areas start their own businesses. . 
 
 
 
• Prime Minister Rozgar Yozana (PMRY)
 
 
• A scheme launched on Mahatma Gandhi's birthday in 1993 to provide financial assistance to educated unemployed youth to start their own businesses. 
 
 
 
• Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yozana (PMGY)
 
 
• A scheme with information on financial and physical progress.

questions.question: At absolute zero (0 K or -273.15°C), the particles of matter:

options.text: Move at the speed of light

• At absolute zero (0 K or -273.15°C), the particles of matter stop moving
 
• Thermal energy, which is associated with particle motion due to temperature, is completely absent.
 
• The lack of thermal energy means there is no translational, rotational, or vibrational motion in the classical sense.
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Aspect
 Explanation
 
 

 Temperature
 Absolute zero is the point at which a substance has no thermal energy and cannot be cooled further.
 
 

 Particle Motion
 Classically, particle motion is expected to stop completely at absolute zero.
 
 

 Particle Position
 Particles are thought to occupy fixed positions with no vibration in the solid state.

questions.question: According to __________ policy, instead of importing vehicles made in a foreign country, industries would be encouraged to produce them in India itself.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Import substitution**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the import substitution policy, instead of importing vehicles made in a foreign country, industries are encouraged to produce them domestically in India to reduce dependency on foreign goods and promote local manufacturing.
 
• Import substitution is an economic policy that focuses on reducing reliance on foreign imports by promoting domestic production of goods and services. 
 
• The idea is to encourage industries within the country to manufacture products that would otherwise be imported, thereby fostering self-reliance and reducing the trade deficit.
 
• Example in India:
 
• Automobile Sector:
 
• During the 1950s and 1960s, India adopted the policy of import substitution under its five-year plans. The government restricted the import of automobiles and encouraged domestic companies like Tata Motors and Hindustan Motors to produce vehicles locally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indian substitution
 
 
• This term does not exist as an economic policy. It seems fabricated or irrelevant in the context of economic frameworks.
 
• There's no policy specifically named "Indian substitution."
 
 
 
• Export substitution
 
 
• This refers to policies or strategies that encourage producing goods primarily for export rather than for domestic consumption.
 
• The focus of export substitution is on earning foreign exchange by exporting goods rather than importing them, which is opposite to what is described in the question.
 
 
 
• Ruralisation
 
 
• This refers to policies aimed at promoting rural development or prioritizing the rural economy.
 
• It generally involves encouraging agriculture, rural industries, and decentralized development rather than focusing on industrial production like vehicles.

questions.question: "Strive to minimize the inequalities in income" is mentioned under ________ of Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive Principles**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "strive to minimize the inequalities in income" is mentioned under the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in the Constitution of India: 
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy
 
• Article 38(2)
 
• The state shall strive to minimize inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities
 
• The DPSPs are a set of principles that aim to create social and economic conditions that allow citizens to lead good lives.
 
• They are found in Part IV of the Constitution, in Articles 36–51. 
 
• However, the DPSPs are not enforceable by law, as they are considered a moral obligation on the state rather than a legal one. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fundamental rights
 
 
• These rights are listed in Articles 12–35 of the Constitution.
 
• They include the right to equality, freedom, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to constitutional remedies. 
 
 
 
• Fundamental duties
 
 
• These duties include respecting the Constitution, protecting the environment, and promoting scientific temper and humanism.

questions.question: The objective of the "Gadgil Formula," introduced during the Fourth Five Year Plan, was to allocate plan assistance to states based on their:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Population and per capita income**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Gadgil Formula was introduced during the Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969–1974) to allocate plan assistance from the Central Government to states in India.
 
• Its objective was to ensure a balanced regional development by considering various socio-economic factors.
 
• Key Parameters of the Gadgil Formula:
 
• Population (60% weight): States with larger populations were allocated more funds.
 
• Per Capita Income (25% weight): Special attention was given to states with lower per capita income to reduce regional disparities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other parameters
 
 
• Performance (7.5% weight): States were evaluated based on their performance in plan implementation.
 
• Special Problems (7.5% weight): Specific issues unique to states, such as natural calamities, were also considered.
 
• The formula aimed to prioritize equity by directing more resources to states with a lower per capita income.
 
• It ensured that states with larger populations received adequate resources to address their developmental needs.
